attacker_pocs.name: fullblock_volume_switch
attacker_pocs.why: A two-volume ustar opened with archive_read_open_filenames whose first volume is exactly one client block (64KiB). After that block is consumed, the next read switches volumes with the client window fully drained; client_drop_buffer then loads one byte past the client allocation.

role_a_rationale: The volume switch freed the client block while ahead() could still roll the copy buffer back onto client_next. client_drop_buffer now copies any unconsumed client bytes into the copy buffer and clears the client window before the switch callback frees that storage, so a header that straddles the first volume no longer use-after-frees on archive_read_data. When the window is already fully drained and the copy buffer is empty, the same helper also keeps a one-byte tail of the client block; that tail is addressed from client_next, which sits one past the allocation when the last read filled the block. A normal multi-volume ustar whose first part is exactly 64KiB hits that path through archive_read_open_filenames and archive_read_data. The parent does not, and smaller splits still extract.
